newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners eye imports as North Sea skids lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners eye imports as North Sea skids lower.

text.p: The sharp fall in North Sea crude premiums was seen likely to pry open the tightly shut import window to the U.S., traders said Tuesday.
Refiners faced with still buoyant operating capacities in efforts to build winter fuel stocks, have recently ignored the possibility of securing Brent-related imports.

"Some sellers have been trying to push Brent to Gulf Coast refiners, but nobody was even nibbling," an East Coast trader said, citing last known offers at West Texas Intermediate + 50-55 cents cif for late Nov. Two Brents traded at Dec Brent -43 and -38 cents fob today, 37 cents below Monday.
A slew of U.K. and Norwegian cargoes reportedly changed hands also at weaker levels in the late U.S. market, confirming the more bearish trend overall.

A trader sold Forties for Nov 13-15 at Dated Brent +15 cents and swapped it for Oseberg, Nov 19-21 at Dated Brent +30 cents. Forties lost 10-15 cents from last week while Oseberg was down a cent from Monday, and five cents from last week.
Two parcels of Statfjord for Nov 13-15 and 9-11 changed hands at Dated Brent +15 cents and flat respectively, compared to a trade at Dated Brent +35 cents last week.
West African and Mediterranean markets were also flush.
Traders said Urals had weakened sharply, with one prompt trade reported at Dated Brent -$1.11 cif Med for Oct 31-Nov 1.

Weaker West African crudes were already drawn into the U.S. yesterday with a U.S. refiner picking up a Cabinda for Nov 23-24 at Dated Brent -$1.67, and the Nemba/Cabinda cargo for Dec 1-5 at Dated Brent -5 cts/-$1.60 fob.
In the U.S. after-market, a handful of paper trades were transacted slightly lower than the London IPE session.
Jan Brent partials moved at $23.20 a barrel, and $23.25 a barrel, down from the $23.33 IPE close.
Brent Dec/Jan intermonth traded at +42 and +43 cents, within the same earlier range of 40-45 cents.
